title: Felix and the Smile
premise: Ivo Villalobos, a property surveyor sent to appraise the derelict Halloway house in the drowned village of Bell Hollow, discovers the house measures him back — rooms that weren't there yesterday, a smile carved into every doorframe that widens each time he lies. When the melted bell of 1911 rings across the valley, the village's few remaining descendants are pulled into the founders' unfinished ritual: seven names must be remembered aloud before the old well refills and drowns what's left of the town. Ivo, who has never believed anything he couldn't measure, must learn that memory is the only instrument that works here — even as the house demands a final name to seal the ritual, and the only name it will accept is his own. In the end Ivo gives his name to the well, saving the found family he never meant to make; they carry his memory out of the valley, and the house, finally measured and released, goes quiet.
about_author: Sable Reyes grew up in a mining town that was flooded for a reservoir, and has spent her career writing about places that refuse to stay underwater. She lives near a lake she does not swim in.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Grief
chapters.summary: Ivo Villalobos arrives in Bell Hollow to appraise the Halloway house, armed with laser measures and professional skepticism. His POV establishes his rigid empiricism and loneliness. The emotional beat is quiet unease: the tape measure returns numbers that don't match themselves.

chapters.title: A House That Appraises Back
chapters.summary: Inside, Ivo finds rooms larger than the exterior allows and a smile carved into every doorframe. When he lies to himself about being fine, the smiles widen. His POV; the beat is denial cracking at the edges as the house begins responding to him personally.

chapters.title: The Descendants
chapters.summary: Ivo meets the last Halloways: gruff matriarch Odile, her grandson Teo who never left, and runaway teen Wren squatting in the chapel. Their found-family dynamic forms around shared dread. Wren's POV; the beat is wary connection between strangers bound by a place.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Teo shows Ivo the dry well behind the house, ringed by seven empty nameplates. The founders' ritual is half-explained through family legend. Ivo's POV; the beat is intellectual fascination curdling into something like fear when the well echoes back his voice before he speaks.

In the parish archive, Wren finds records of the bell's melting and a photograph of seven founders whose faces blur identically. One founder's diary describes 'finishing the naming' before winter. Wren's POV; the beat is the thrill of discovery shadowed by the diary's final unfinished sentence.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings
chapters.summary: At dusk, the bell melted in 1911 rings across the valley. Every descendant hears their childhood nickname in its tone. The village's scattered survivors converge on the Halloway house without deciding to. Multiple POVs braided; the beat is involuntary gathering, like iron filings to a magnet.

chapters.title: Seven Names
chapters.summary: Odile reveals the ritual: the founders named seven things to keep the water out — but the seventh name was never spoken, and the well has been slowly refilling ever since. Ivo refuses to believe. His POV; the beat is his skepticism weaponized against him as the house punishes doubt.

chapters.title: Rooms That Weren't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: The house grows a nursery containing Ivo's own forgotten childhood belongings from a home he's never mentioned. Teo witnesses it. Teo's POV; the beat is horror turning intimate — the house isn't haunted by the past, it's collecting theirs.

chapters.title: First Name: Water
chapters.summary: Following the diary, the group speaks the first founder's name at the well. The water level visibly drops an inch. Hope flickers. Wren's POV; the beat is fragile triumph immediately undercut by the well whispering a countdown only children can hear.

chapters.title: The Smile Widens
chapters.summary: Ivo lies to protect Wren from a terrible truth about her grandmother, and every carved smile in the house stretches toward screaming. The house feeds on falsehood. Ivo's POV; the beat is guilt made architectural, forcing him toward honesty as survival strategy.

chapters.title: Second and Third Names
chapters.summary: Two more names spoken; two more inches lost. But each speaker loses a specific memory as payment — Odile forgets her wedding day, Teo forgets his mother's face. Teo's POV; the beat is the theme crystallizing: the price of survival is paid in remembering less.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren secretly offers the well her worst memory instead of a precious one. The well accepts it hungrily — too hungrily — and takes three. She can no longer remember why she ran away, or why she's crying. Wren's POV; the beat is grief without an object.

chapters.title: Fourth Name: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: The fourth name belongs to a founder whose descendants all died. The group must sing it, and the house sings back in voices under water. Ivo's POV; the beat is awe breaking through disbelief — he cannot explain this, and for the first time stops trying.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile admits the Halloways stopped the ritual deliberately in 1911: the seventh name was a person, and her great-grandmother refused to give one up. The refilling well is a debt accruing interest. Odile's POV; the beat is generational guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Fifth Name: Flood Season
chapters.summary: Rain begins falling only over the house. The fifth name buys them days, not peace. The village road floods, trapping everyone together. Multiple POVs; the beat is forced intimacy — the found family solidifies because there is nowhere else to be.

chapters.title: Sixth Name and the Empty Plate
chapters.summary: Six names spoken, six plates filled. The seventh plate remains blank and now bears Ivo's initials, freshly carved. He understands what the house has been measuring him for. Ivo's POV; the beat is cold clarity — the appraisal was always of him.

chapters.title: What Ivo Won't Give
chapters.summary: Ivo attempts to cheat the ritual with a false name. The house retaliates: it erases him from documents, photographs, memories — Wren looks at him without recognition. His POV; the beat is terror of unbeing, worse than death, proving how much he now wants to belong.

chapters.title: The Night the Well Refills
chapters.summary: Water rises through the floors; the drowned choir sings from below the floorboards. The group makes their stand in the nursery, holding hands around the well mouth. Teo's POV; the beat is desperate solidarity on the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: Seventh Name
chapters.summary: At the waterline, Ivo speaks his own true name — freely, honestly, the first fully honest act of his life. The well stills. The house exhales. His POV; the beat is transcendence through surrender, belief achieved at the moment of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Quiet House
chapters.summary: The flood recedes. The house stands ordinary, measurable, its doorframe smiles faded to wood grain. The survivors walk out into morning light carrying objects Ivo left behind. Wren's POV; the beat is hollow relief and the ache of a missing person no record confirms.

chapters.title: Remembering Aloud
chapters.summary: The found family performs a counter-ritual of their own invention: speaking Ivo's name and story aloud at the well each season, refusing to let memory be the price. Odile carves an eighth nameplate. Teo's POV; the beat is defiance — love as an act of preservation.

chapters.title: Felix and the Smile
chapters.summary: Years later, Wren brings her young son Felix to the quiet house. He points to a doorframe where, only for him, a small smile remains — and waves at someone unseen. Final image: somewhere beneath, a name is held, warm and remembered. Wren's POV; the beat is bittersweet peace, the price honored rather than escaped.
